## Purpose and Runtime

PrivateAgent is a Flutter Android application that translates text, voice, or Telegram commands into multi-step automation across installed apps. Its core loop combines an LLM provider with Android Accessibility APIs: inspect current UI, ask the model for the next action, execute it natively, and repeat. Primary Flutter entry points are `lib/main.dart` and the overlay entry point `lib/overlay_main.dart`; Android starts through `android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/orailnoor/privateagent/MainActivity.kt`.

## UI, Onboarding, and User Control

Flutter screens expose command interaction, setup, configuration, and history. Onboarding guides required Android accessibility permissions; settings holds AI-provider and Telegram configuration; the home screen is the primary interactive surface. Key paths: `lib/screens/home_screen.dart`, `lib/screens/onboarding_screen.dart`, `lib/screens/settings_screen.dart`. Feature availability is gated centrally in `lib/config/feature_flags.dart`.

## Task Models and Execution Orchestration

The task domain is represented by actions, chat messages, and reusable saved skills. `TaskExecutor` is the likely orchestration boundary for a requested task, while `ActionHandler` dispatches individual AI-selected operations and recovery handles failure/retry behavior. Relevant paths: `lib/models/agent_action.dart`, `lib/services/task_executor.dart`, `lib/services/action_handler.dart`, `lib/services/recovery_engine.dart`.

## AI Decision and Feedback Loop

`AIService` is the external-model boundary, expected to package task context, screen state, and prior action result for DeepSeek/OpenRouter-compatible APIs. Its output becomes `AgentAction` data, which the execution layer performs; subsequent screen inspection feeds the next iteration. Conversation and persistent skill context are managed separately through `lib/services/chat_history_service.dart` and `lib/services/skill_memory_service.dart`. The principal paths are `lib/services/ai_service.dart`, `lib/models/chat_message.dart`, and `lib/models/saved_skill.dart`.

## Native Android Automation Boundary

Android Accessibility is the privileged actuator and UI-reader boundary. The declared service and its accessibility metadata are in `android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/orailnoor/privateagent/AgentAccessibilityService.kt` and `android/app/src/main/res/xml/accessibility_service_config.xml`. Flutter-facing automation abstractions include `lib/services/screen_automation_service.dart` and `lib/services/system_control_service.dart`. This boundary requires user-enabled Accessibility Service permissions and is Android-specific.

## Command Inputs, Remote Control, and Device Integrations

Commands can originate locally, through speech recognition, or Telegram polling. Telegram is an external Bot API integration rather than an application backend; it forwards remote task commands and likely progress. Device-facing services cover voice, notifications, contacts, alarms, and app launch. Core paths: `lib/services/telegram_service.dart`, `lib/services/voice_service.dart`, `lib/services/communication_service.dart`, `lib/services/notification_service.dart`, and `lib/services/app_launcher_service.dart`.

## Overlay and Platform Plugins

A separate Flutter overlay runtime supports persistent on-screen agent UI over other apps, backed by a vendored Android foreground/overlay plugin: `lib/overlay_main.dart`, `local_plugins/flutter_overlay_window/lib/flutter_overlay_window.dart`, and `local_plugins/flutter_overlay_window/android/src/main/java/flutter/overlay/window/flutter_overlay_window/OverlayService.java`. A second local method-channel plugin bridges custom native functions via `local_plugins/agent_native/lib/agent_native_method_channel.dart` and `local_plugins/agent_native/android/src/main/kotlin/com/example/agent_native/AgentNativePlugin.kt`.

## Build and Release Infrastructure

The deployable target is Android/Flutter, built with Gradle Kotlin DSL under `android/app/build.gradle.kts`. Automated Android release packaging is defined in `.github/workflows/android-release.yml`. Runtime dependencies include Android API 26+, Accessibility Services, LLM HTTP APIs (DeepSeek/OpenRouter), Telegram Bot API polling, and native speech-to-text.
